summary: The facility ban (SB 8, the 'Texas Women's Privacy Act', effective 4 Dec 2025) is actually enforced: within 48 hours (6 Dec 2025), DPS troopers checked IDs at women's restrooms in the Capitol and issued criminal-trespass warnings to four trans women, banning them from the Capitol for a year; the Attorney General opened the first state bathroom-law enforcement inquiry against Austin ISD (Mar 2026) and escalated it with a second records demand (27 Apr 2026), and a North Texas graduate student was formally 'investigated' under the law (Feb 2026). Highest absolute toll of killings of trans women in the country (44 recorded 2008–2025; 7.6 per 100k/yr); 66 anti-LGBTQ incidents in 2025 (3rd-highest US total). Rated 'Do Not Travel' — the harshest tier — in the July 2026 legal-risk assessment. Well below the national score 0.36.

sources.summary: Reports the first week of enforcement of SB 8 (Women's Privacy Act, in effect 4 Dec 2025): opponents' test of the law met with ID checks at women's restrooms in the Capitol, while the Austin City Council moved to circumvent the law's intent; colleges and cities implement divergent policies and questions remain about how the law can be enforced.

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (HTTP 403); the underlying local-TV report covers DPS giving one-year bans and criminal-trespass warnings to four transgender women after a Capitol rally against the restroom law (6 Dec 2025) — the dossier's source for the 'within 48 hours' enforcement fact.

Attorney General Paxton escalated his inquiry into Austin ISD (27 Apr 2026) with a second records demand over allegations a student used a bathroom inconsistent with their sex assigned at birth, after a March investigation opened via a state tip-line complaint alleging an SB 8 violation — the first state 'bathroom law' enforcement inquiry of its kind.

State-by-state Trans Murder Monitoring analysis (2008–2025, US 428 recorded victims, 90% trans women): Texas carries the largest state count (44 recorded killings; 7.6 per 100k trans women/yr) alongside the worst-law group generally, with all rates framed as undercount floors.

July 2026 edition of the widely cited Anti-Trans National Legal Risk Assessment Map: Idaho becomes the fourth-ever 'Do Not Travel' state (bathroom usage can lead to 5-year prison sentences); the adult-risk tiering places Texas and Florida among 'Do Not Travel' and South Carolina at 'Worst Laws Passed', with methodology based on law-by-law expert assessment.

tangentialFactors: LGB-facing visibility is rolling back too: Arlington's city council rescinded its LGBTQ non-discrimination ordinance (Dec 2025) and Arlington Pride suspended its 2026 events; a Houston-area venue pulled out of Katy Pride under school-board pressure.
localsOnly: Document governance is resident-facing but nationally anomalous: DPS has ignored court-ordered gender-marker changes and built a database of applicants seeking them.
